At the full sample only 105 chords have an interior weight (5 rules faster than v3w by point x 21 slower by point). The other 115 are clamped (97 at w = 0, 18 at w = 1) and their point value equals one competitor's E; only their intervals differ. Of the 20 smallest-lower-bound chords, 14 have w = 0.000 and a point of +9.93, which is lr400_16_1's own E. review.summary:
Label: measure. The PASS reading itself stands, so I found no blocker. On the stored rows the total close-following count (ttc_net) is what it claims to be, and v3w's edge is not an exposure artefact: normalising by vehicle-seconds, vehicle-km or vehicles passed leaves it unchanged. It is not a 1-Hz aliasing effect either (the half-second offset sample gives the same edge), and it is larger for severe events than for mild ones. The interpretation does need to change, and three findings are major:
(1) Against the weakest competitor, lr400_16_1, all of the edge sits at the two 300-m on-ramp acceleration lanes. Away from both merges v3w has MORE close-following (-8.6 % [-14.7, -1.4]). It is not shown better than grid_lr400_13_1 there (+4.6 [-2.2, +12.8]). Neither V530 nor the §4 template states this. The C1 screen created its K3 'merges only' rule for exactly this case.
(2) The merge part of the edge tracks lane-end stops on those short lanes. Paired seed differences correlate at rho 0.85-0.90. Check (a) showed these stops largely vanish when the ramp-2 lane is longer, and merge-2 close-following then falls 35-98 %. Merge 2 carries 40-75 % of each competitor's edge and merges 1+2 together 57-103 %, so the length label applies to the headline number, not only to 'merge-2 readings'. Merge 1 (also 300 m) was never length-checked.
(3) 76-104 % of the edge falls in the period that starts 120 s after the slowdown ends. During the taper and hold of the slowdown, v3w has more close-following than lr400_16_1 (-47 %) and grid_lr400_13_1 (-39 %), and is not shown different from MPC-F.
The minor findings are about units and wording, the undisclosed fact that v3w's reward penalises this same TTC<3 s flag, and V&V gaps (PR-23 partial, PR-24 and PR-28 gaps, merge-conflict safety listed as 'Not for'). All my numbers are descriptive and post hoc. I computed them with the reader's statistic (5 learners, joint bootstrap B=20,000, rng 20261108, 97.5 %) on the stored rows. Scripts and outputs are in /tmp/claude-1000/-srv-shared-Workspace-phd-phd-speed-harmo-v5b1/2d269ac5-95be-4f04-801b-ec9cc9873355/scratchpad/cfv/measure/ (extract.py, cd5.py, a1-a6.py, a1.out-a6.out). No simulation was run, and no repository file was edited.
checked: My statistic reproduces the reader exactly: E lr400_16_1 +9.9 [+6.2, +15.0], away -8.6 [-14.7, -1.4] (a1.out vs cf_screen/screen.json readings).

Counter definition (read only): ttc_net = E30 + out_E30 (plant_sweep.py:397). E30 is the merge-1 area only: 2_0 tail, 3a_0, 3a_1, 3_0 head (b_env.py:277-296). out_E30 = the network count minus that area (b_env.py:423-425). So ttc_net is the whole-network count. The counter name E30 is unrelated to the cell name E30.

Formula: per vehicle on the network, once per simulated second, after warm-up (the 300 s warm-up loop at b_env.py:179 does not count; window 300-1800 s, 1500 steps per row). The leader is SUMO getLeader(v, 200): the same lane, then the best-lane continuation (sumo-src MSVehicle.cpp:6755-6780). gap = returned gap + minGap = bumper to bumper. A sample counts if dv > 0 and gap/dv < 3.0 (TTC_REWARD, b_env.py:31, 311). Unit: follower-seconds (1-Hz samples), not events. Adjacent-lane and merging-into-gap conflicts are not counted. Followers without a leader or with dv <= 0 are not counted, and neither are pending vehicles.
Consistency on all 14,880 rows (a2 check): ttc3 (plant_sweep.py:213-232 conflicts) == ttc_net == m_ttc3_all == sum of m_road_ttc3 groups.

The smallest advantage, about 10 % (lower bound 6 %), is against an untuned look-ahead rule, lr400_16_1. Hard braking is lower than for most rules but not all, and hard-braking events are more frequent than under the close-following-searched rules. No rule was tuned on this event; a rule tuned there could close the gap. The result does not speak to delay gains, other events, demands or automated shares, real roads, or online adaptation. It is one cell out of 95 tested on this plant, in a line whose broader studies (Plan B in TRUCK, conf3b in X2) did not confirm a combined delay and close-following win.
